Lakers Could Add Klay Thompson Following Latest Update
description: Former Warriors guard Klay Thompson has long been connected to the Lakers, but it seems more possible than ever that he could join LA. The post Lakers Could Add Klay Thompson Following Latest Update appeared first on LA Sports Report.
fullText:
Former Golden State Warriors guard Klay Thompson has long been connected to the Lakers, but in the twilight of his career, it seems more possible than ever that he could join LA.

Thompson has a natural connection to the Lakers, being the son of Mychal Thompson, a longtime Laker and true fan favorite.

Klay was a mainstay with the Warriors for a very long time, and even when he hit free agency, he chose to sign with the Mavericks rather than join the Lakers, passing up a real chance to join LA.

Recently, Mychal shared that he is "trying" to get Klay to sign with the Lakers, joining Doncic in LA this time and serving as a shooter on the wing.

While Klay is not currently a free agent, he is under contract for one more year, earning $17.4 million. There are rumors of a possible buyout or trade away from the Mavericks, looking to help a team on a contender.

After talk of a buyout, the Mavs reportedly want to instead work out a trade to avoid paying part of Thompson's salary and possibly get any kind of assets.

Thompson, a three-point shooting specialist, has gone through knee and leg injuries that have sapped a good part of his athleticism.

His play was so poor upon his comeback that the Warriors and Thompson made the call to move on.

The Dallas Mavericks, looking to get over the hump in the postseason with Luka Doncic, decided to pursue Thompson and signed him to a big free-agent contract.

However, things changed quickly for the Mavs; they ended up trading Doncic and going through a full rebuild, and they are now led by second-year player Cooper Flagg.

With the Mavs, Thompson has still shot the ball well, though his points have been on a decline, along with his field goal attempts per game.

Last year, he played 69 games, started only eight games, and put up 11.7 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.

Thompson, one of the greatest shooters of all time, shot 39.1% in 2024 and 38.3% last year from deep.

The Lakers need help on the wings, and a change of scenery, alongside an established role on a competitor, could be what Thompson needs to get his career going again.

At 36 and with so many surgeries, he may not have much juice left, but if he does, the Lakers could use him.

LA may be more willing to sign him following a buyout rather than trade for him, but they will likely be inquiring to see how viable adding Thompson is.

title: Double Impact: Phillies 7, Nationals 3
description: And you get a double! And YOU get a double! Everyone gets a double!
fullText:
The Phillies offense pounded out eight doubles on 16 total hits to dispatch the Nationals and take the four-game series with a final score of 7-3. It was the most doubles Philadelphia has had in a game since September 6th of 2024 when they also had eight in a game against Marlins. Bryson Stott led the way with two doubles while Luis Arraez, Alec Bohm, J.T. Realmuto, Trea Turner, Bryce Harper, and Brandon Marsh rounded out the collection. Meanwhile on the mound, Cristopher Sánchez wasn't his sharpest but was able to finish five innings and allowed just two runs.

The first two bagger came in the first inning courtesy of Luis Arraez, who continues to make an impact offensively in his first few games with the Phillies. He doubled in Trea Turner and moved Bryce Harper to third after they had reached on a single and a walk respectively.

Your first look at Luis Arraez in powder blue ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/RnRZ38C5I5

Alec Bohm quickly followed with the Phillies second double of the night, driving in Harper to push the lead to 2-0. Arraez tried to score from second, but despite hurdling the tag attempt by Washington catcher Keibert Ruiz, was not able to touch home plate and was called out.

The next double came to lead off the third, with J.T. Realmuto ripping one down the third base line off of Nats' starter Miles Mikolas. Bryson Stott then grounded out to third to advance Realmuto before Justin Crawford bounced a worm burner over the head of the drawn in first baseman for a base hit and an RBI, extending the then lead to 3-1.

J. Craw gets one more on the scoreboard! pic.twitter.com/2iARQWiGQl

Double number four came two batters later, when Turner hit a ball off the wall that Crawford likely should have scored on, but the rookie appeared to hesitate going into second base and was ultimately thrown out at home to end the inning, becoming the second runner to be gunned down at the plate in as many innings for the Phillies.

Harper got in on the fun to begin the third inning, lining the Phillies' fifth double of the game down the right field line. Arraez then hit a fly ball to the warning track that should have allowed Harper to tag up and go to third, but Harper appeared to misread it and did not advance. Bohm then lined out putting the run in jeopardy, but Brandon Marsh came through with double number six, a sharp 105 MPH line drive to right that scored Harper and pushed the lead to 4-1.

Prepare for trouble!
Make it double! pic.twitter.com/wKFc00gEy5

Realmuto knocked in Marsh with a run of the mill two-out single before Stott notched double number seven to right to give the Phillies a 6-1 lead. Stott later led off the sixth inning with his second and the Phillies' eighth double of the night and eventually came around to score after a Crawford bunt set up a Kyle Schwarber RBI single to give Philadelphia it's seventh run of the ballgame.

Schwarbs picks up his second hit of the game! pic.twitter.com/lxGGMvKocr

Cristopher Sánchez struggled with command all night despite only issuing two walks. He needed 98 pitches to get through five innings and had to escape multiple jams. The first such instance came in the third when Esteury Ruiz and Dylan Crews led off the inning with back-to-back singles when the score was 3-1 Phillies. But Sánchez was able to bear down and get Andrés Chaparro to ground into a double play before striking out Brady House swinging to extinguish the threat.

Sánchez ended his night with another tightrope act in the fifth, when the Nats loaded the bases on a Brady House walk with one out in a 6-2 game. But once again, Sánchez was able to settle down and prevent further damage by striking out CJ Abrams and inducing a groundout against Harry Ford to end the inning. The Phillies southpaw ended his night with five innings pitched, two runs, six hits including a home run, two walks, and six strikeouts.

Sánchez' early exit required the Phillies taxed bullpen to once again throw four innings a night after eight relievers pitched in an extra-innings game. Orion Kerkering was first up and allowed one run on two hits but collected three strikeouts. That would be all the bullpen allowed, as José Alvarado, Jonathan Bowlan, and Jhoan Duran would combine to throw three perfect innings with three total strikeouts in relief to preserve the series win.

The Phillies will send Zack Wheeler (10-2, 2.49) to the mound against the Blue Jays and newly acquired starter José Soriano (9-6, 3.29). First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 PM. Chase Utley will be inducted into the Phillies Wall of Fame with a pre-game ceremony to begin Alumni Weekend.

title: Browns Eyeing New Receiver Ahead of Preseason Opener
description: The Cleveland Browns are looking to add some new weapons. The post Browns Eyeing New Receiver Ahead of Preseason Opener appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns are taking a closer look at their options at wide receiver ahead of their preseason opener.

Cleveland worked out seven free agents on Thursday, including receivers Romello Brinson, Stephon Johnson and Ben Patterson, according to the NFL transaction wire.

The Browns also brought in defensive tackle Evan Anderson, guard Joshua Gray, defensive back Jeadyn Lukus and offensive tackle Raiqwon O'Neal.

With three receivers included in the workout, Cleveland appears interested in adding more competition to a crowded but largely unproven position group. The Browns open their preseason schedule against the Chicago Bears on August 15.

GettyRomello Brinson of the Southern Methodist Mustangs reacts prior to a game against the Penn State Nittany Lions. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images)

Brinson is the most accomplished receiver among the three players Cleveland evaluated. The former SMU standout caught 43 passes for 638 yards and three touchdowns during his final college season. He averaged 14.8 yards per reception and produced a pair of 100-yard performances.

Johnson averaged 21.2 yards per catch during an injury-shortened final season at Houston, finishing with 13 receptions for 275 yards and two touchdowns in five games. He finished his college career with 69 receptions for 954 yards and seven touchdowns.

Patterson is the biggest target of the group at 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds. He initially signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars as an undrafted free agent after finishing his career at Division II Texas-Permian Basin.

None of the three would enter Cleveland as a favorite to make the final roster. However, a strong showing during the remainder of training camp and the preseason could put any of them in consideration for a reserve role or practice-squad spot.

The Browns overhauled their receiving corps after getting limited production from the passing game last season. Cleveland used high draft picks on KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, giving the offense two young playmakers to develop alongside Jerry Jeudy. Isaiah Bond also returns after catching 18 passes for 338 yards as a rookie.

Cedric Tillman, Tylan Wallace, Malachi Corley and Jamari Thrash are among the other receivers competing for roster spots.

Jeudy remains the established leader of the group, but the roles behind him are unsettled. Concepcion and Boston carry significant expectations and have made an early impression in camp. Bond flashed big-play potential last season but remains relatively unproven.

The Browns also recently lost some depth when rookie Aaron Anderson suffered an undisclosed injury. Cleveland opens the preseason against the Bears before hosting the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 22 and the New England Patriots on Aug. 27.

title: LSU football freshman making plays, other notes from fall camp
description: Through two practices, this is what has stood out so far for LSU football at fall camp.
fullText:
BATON ROUGE — LSU football hit the practice fields for the second time for fall camp on Aug. 6.

First year head coach Lane Kiffin and his staff continued to the preseason work with the Tigers before they take on Clemson in the 2026 season opener at Tiger Stadium Saturday, Sept. 5. Media got to view two periods of Thursday evening's session in which the team wore shoulders pads for the first time this preseason.

After two days, here are a few things that have stuck for LSU at fall camp.

LANE KIFFIN ON SAM LEAVITT Why Lane Kiffin said LSU QB Sam Leavitt looked his best in 1st camp practice

From day one to day two, LSU junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt looked better in the deep ball department. On Wednesday, some of the deeper throws were a shade off target. But Thursday evening, the deep shots were on target, completing a nice over-the-shoulder throw to Winston Watkins on a go route.

The intermediate and short throws have been near perfect for Leavitt so far, so to see some improvement in the timing and placement of deep throws is a positive sign for the quarterback who is making his way back from foot surgery.

Sophomore tailback and Wisconsin transfer Dilin Jones continues to lead the running back group during drills at practice. Behind him are sophomores Caden Durham than Harlem Berry.

Jones has been consistent since he's arrived on campus before spring ball began and he's having a solid start to fall camp. Expectation remains as of now that he'll be LSU's starting tailback come September.

Lamar Brown is making himself get noticed out there. In the 12 minutes media were able to watch practice, the Baton Rouge native and freshman defensive end made a tackle for loss in a drill that featured the full 11 on defense.

Kiffin said following the team's opening practice Wednesday that the coaches anticipate the speed of game and learning the playbook and all to take some time for Brown, but there's excitement because he can do a number of things.

But like he showed Thursday, in the instinctual department, Brown has the skill and ability to make plays. Brown is currently lining up at defensive end with the defense's second team.

For the second straight day, freshman Jhase Thomas lined up at one of the starting safety positions. Junior Tamarcus Cooley, who started all 13 games for the Tigers a season ago, worked with the second unit again.

Thomas is surprising media members by overtaking Cooley for the position to this point. The question is will be maintain it and earn the start against Clemson.

Behind Leavitt, there's still some work to be done for Husan Longstreet and Landen Clark. Through two days of fall camp, both have been hit-and-miss in the intermediate and deep shots down the field.

In red zone work Thursday, both were off target on some easy throws. On the deeper throws, Longstreet has been more accurate, especially on throws over the middle of the formation. Longstreet has been working as the primary backup to Leavitt in fall camp so far.

Cory Diaz covers the LSU Tigers for The Daily Advertiser as part of the USA TODAY Network. Follow his Tigers coverage on Twitter: @ByCoryDiaz. Got questions regarding LSU athletics? Send them to Cory Diaz at bdiaz@gannett.com.

title: Larry Fitzgerald gets emotional speaking about father ahead of Hall of Fame induction
description: Larry Fitzgerald reflected on what his late father, Larry Fitzgerald Sr., meant to him ahead of his Pro Football Hall of fame induction.
fullText:
For Larry Fitzgerald, his Pro Football Hall of Fame induction will be extra emotional because his father, Larry Fitzgerald Sr. won't be with him. Fitzgerald Sr. was a renowned journalist and sports radio host based in Minneapolis known as "The Original." He passed away in June.

The Arizona Cardinals legend appeared on NBC's pregame show for the Hall of Fame Game on Thursday, Aug. 6 and spoke about his father, who was originally going to be the person to present him in Canton.

"There is no journey without him, the sacrifices that he made, every door he opened," Fitzgerald said as he choked up. "I know he's here with me. I can feel his presence. It's still very emotional, but I'm so happy I had a father that great for 42 years."

"There is no journey without him."@LarryFitzgerald couldn't be more grateful for his late father and everything he did for him ❤️@ProFootballHOF Game on NBC
Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/7z23NHzNp7

Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin chimed in with his memorial to Fitzgerald Sr. The two knew each other from back when Tomlin was the defensive coordinator for the Minnesota Vikings in the 2000s.

"I had the pleasure to get to know him from my time in Minnesota," he said, "and most certainly, he's here with you and most certainly, he's smiling at all of us right now."

Fitzgerald finished his 17-year NFL career second all-time with 17,492 receiving yards. He set Cardinals franchise records for receiving yards, catches (1,432) and touchdowns (31). He was named to 11 Pro Bowls and was the third overall pick of the 2004 NFL Draft after starring at Pittsburgh.

Fitzgerald will be inducted as a member of the Class of 2026 with Drew Brees, Adam Vinatieri, Luke Kuechly and Roger Craig on Saturday, Aug. 8.

title: Rodri chooses Barcelona over Real Madrid as Manchester City exit takes shape — report
description: The Spanish midfielder has informed the club that his preference is Barcelona
fullText:
Bar another dramatic turnaround, Real Madrid's pursuit of Rodri appears to be over.

The Manchester City midfielder has informed Madrid that his preference, should he leave England this summer, is to join Barcelona. Until recently, Madrid had been considered the more realistic destination for Rodri, and the club had made a significant financial proposal to the player. But there had been doubts throughout the process over how convinced Rodri actually was about moving to the Bernabéu which partly stem from Real Madrid not pulling the trigger quick enough, taking too long to close out the deal thinking they had time (and also no competition from other clubs).

But their hesitancy has now cost them. Rodri has given Barcelona permission to formally approach Manchester City and explore the conditions of a transfer. No agreement between the clubs exists yet, but the situation has changed considerably: Barça can now move from maintaining an interest in the background to actually negotiating a deal — with Rodri seemingly convinced by phone calls from Hansi Flick as well as Spanish National Team teammates.

From Madrid's perspective, there appears to be little appetite convincing Rodri to changes his mind.

The club's position has traditionally been fairly straightforward in situations like this: if a player needs significant convincing to join Real Madrid, particularly when another club is his preferred destination, Madrid are generally comfortable moving on. Rodri was highly rated internally by some members of Real Madrid's board for obvious reasons — his quality in possession, tactical intelligence, leadership and experience would have filled an important role in José Mourinho's midfield — but there was never complete confidence at Valdebebas that Madrid was where he genuinely wanted to be.

Or at least that's the story the club will want to push out now. Some sources state that Florentino Perez wasn't truly convinced of Rodri because of his injury history and age, otherwise he would've wrapped up the deal weeks ago.

Madrid had held two conversations with Manchester City regarding Rodri, although neither progressed past the negotiation stage.

AS reported that Rodri explained his reasoning to Madrid during recent conversations, and most of it appears to have been football-related.

Barcelona's style was one factor. Rodri has spent the majority of his prime playing under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, where his responsibilities as the deepest midfielder go considerably beyond conventional defensive-midfield work. He dictates possession, controls the tempo of games, positions himself as an outlet during buildup and has spent years operating in a system built around positional superiority.

There are obvious differences between Guardiola's City and Hansi Flick's Barcelona, but the basic principles in possession are familiar enough that Rodri can see a natural fit.

There is also a personal element. Rodri has developed relationships with several Barcelona players through the Spanish national team and reportedly feels a greater affinity with that group. Guardiola's connection to Barcelona and the footballing education Rodri has received at City also contributed to his preference.

None of those reasons are particularly difficult to understand.

In fact, stylistically, Barcelona may be the cleaner fit.

Madrid could absolutely use Rodri, but Mourinho would not necessarily ask him to play the same way he has under Guardiola. Madrid's midfield is also going through its own evolution and, after an extremely active summer in the transfer market, there are several ways Mourinho can configure it without adding another player on enormous wages.

Madrid liked Rodri, but they didn't like him enough to persuade him to choose them over the club he actually wanted.

Barcelona's interest did not suddenly emerge this week.

They had been monitoring Rodri's situation for several weeks while keeping their distance because Madrid appeared to have the advantage. Barcelona's primary transfer target remains Julián Álvarez, but the possibility of signing Rodri was considered significant enough for the club to maintain contact with his camp and stay informed about developments.

Their strategy was essentially to wait.

If Rodri reached an agreement with Madrid, there wasn't much Barcelona could realistically do. If those talks stalled and the midfielder became available, they wanted to be positioned to move quickly.

That is where things stand now.

Barcelona had previously stopped short of submitting an offer either to Rodri or Manchester City. With the player now giving them permission to proceed, they can begin discussions with City Football Group CEO Ferran Soriano over what a transfer would require.

Reports in Spain have put the potential fee at approximately €60 million, with Barcelona prepared to offer Rodri a four-year contract worth around €30 million gross annually.

That would obviously be a major financial commitment for a 30-year-old midfielder, but Rodri's contractual situation gives Barcelona some leverage.

He has one year remaining on his Manchester City deal and has so far declined the club's attempts to extend it. City therefore have a fairly simple decision to make: reach another renewal agreement, sell him this summer, or risk losing one of the best midfielders in the world for nothing in 2027.

The reported €60 million price has to be viewed through that context.

For a player of Rodri's level, it would ordinarily look low. For a 30-year-old entering the final year of his contract and apparently prepared to leave, the market is different.

Another significant part of the situation is what City are doing themselves.

The English club have reportedly reached a verbal agreement with Ayyoub Bouaddi, the highly rated young midfielder who has been identified as a possible successor to Rodri. Bouaddi is valued at around €60 million.

That doesn't guarantee Rodri will leave, but City identifying and advancing on a replacement is an obvious indication that they are preparing for the possibility.

Rodri has little left to accomplish in England. He has won the Premier League repeatedly, the Champions League and virtually every other major trophy available at club level. He also enters this decision with his status in Spanish football higher than ever after being named the best player at the most recent World Cup.

The question is no longer whether he has established himself at City.

It is whether he wants to spend the final elite years of his career somewhere else.

Everything at the moment points toward yes.

And if that somewhere is Barcelona, City's leverage becomes increasingly limited. A player with one year remaining on his contract can exert considerable influence over his destination simply by refusing alternatives.

There is no point pretending Rodri wouldn't have been an excellent signing for Real Madrid.

He would have solved several problems immediately.

Madrid have spent years trying to replace different components of the Casemiro-Kroos-Modrić midfield rather than finding direct replacements for those players, which is probably the correct approach because those profiles are almost impossible to replicate individually.

Rodri would have given Mourinho something different.

He is one of the best midfielders in the world at receiving under pressure, organizing possession and controlling where a game is played. He provides defensive positioning without sacrificing technical quality and can dictate games without needing to constantly advance into the final third.

That kind of player becomes particularly useful in Champions League knockout games, where controlling five or 10 chaotic minutes can be as valuable as creating another scoring opportunity.

His leadership also mattered to Madrid. Rodri is an established figure for Spain and has the personality to walk into an elite dressing room without needing time to establish credibility.

There is a reason Madrid explored the signing.

But there is also a difference between recognizing that Rodri improves the team and deciding that Madrid should do everything possible to sign a 30-year-old midfielder to a four-year contract worth around €30 million gross per season.

Once the player himself preferred Barcelona, the decision became easier.

Mourinho has been kept informed throughout the process and reportedly believes Madrid already have solutions in the squad.

If Mourinho genuinely feels that way, his theory will now be tested.

Madrid have plenty of midfield talent, although nobody currently provides exactly the same combination of control, positioning and distribution that Rodri would have brought. Aurélien Tchouaméni is the most obvious defensive-midfield option, while Federico Valverde and Eduardo Camavinga can provide different qualities depending on the structure around them — but Camavinga has been poor for quite some time, and there are big questions on how Valverde and Tchouameni can fit together. Real Madrid will have to rely on Arda Güler and Bernardo Silve to help control games.

The important distinction is that Madrid don't necessarily need to find a player who plays like Rodri. They need to solve the problems Rodri would have solved. Those are different things.

Tchouaméni can provide more physical coverage. Valverde can compensate with running and ball progression. Camavinga gives Madrid press resistance and carrying, Güler and Silva can help control play. Mourinho can also alter the structure around whichever player operates deepest, rather than asking one midfielder to reproduce everything Rodri does for City.

title: Top prospect Jefferson Rojas gets first hit in Mets system, Billy Amick leads offensive onslaught for Double-A Binghamton
description: It was a great day for the Mets prospects down in Double-A on Thursday, with Jefferson Rojas, Mitch Voit and Billy Amick contributing to 22 runs for the Rumble Ponies.
fullText:
It was a great day for the Mets prospects down in Double-A on Thursday.

The Rumble Ponies exploded for 23 runs in their 23-3 win over Hartford. The 19 runs set a franchise record for Binghamton and many of the Mets' top prospects -- most arriving at the trade deadline -- contributed to that score.

Voit, No. 5 in Joe DeMayo's list of Mets prospects, went 5-for-6 with a walk and two RBI. In eight games since being promoted to Double-A, Voit is 19-for-27 with a home run and eight RBI. He tied Binghamton's single-game record with five hits.

Jefferson Rojas, the centerpiece in the Clay Holmes deal and the Mets' new No. 1 prospect, got off the schneid, picking up his first hit in his second game in the Mets' system. The shortstop finished 1-for-4 with a walk and a run scored.

Billy Amick, who came over from the Twins in the A.J. Minter deal, was the big run producer in this one. The third baseman went 3-for-4 with a walk and six RBI. Two of Amick's three hits were home runs.

Thursday was Amick's fifth game with Binghamton and he is 6-for-18 with three home runs and eight RBI since arriving in the Mets system.

On the pitching side, Gary Gill Hill, who was traded to the Mets from the Rays in the Freddy Peralta deal, had a solid Binghamton debut.

The right-hander pitched five scoreless innings, allowing three hits and walking two while striking out four to pick up the win. Entering Thursday's game, the 21-year-old pitched to a 7-3 record, a 4.49 ERA and a 1.38 WHIP across 20 starts.

title: Mike Tomlin champions Steelers legend’s HOF case in NBC debut
description: Mike Tomlin advocated for the inclusion to the Hall of Fame of an absolute legend of the Pittsburgh Steelers.
fullText:
Mike Tomlin champions Steelers legend's HOF case in NBC debut appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Mike Tomlin was back on the field on Thursday, not as a coach, but as an analyst for NBC. He made his television debut for the Hall of Fame Game between the Carolina Panthers and the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio.

Tomlin transitioned to broadcasting after resigning from the Pittsburgh Steelers in January following their exit in the wild-card round of the playoffs.

Tomlin will be forever loyal to Pittsburgh, which he led to the championship in 2009. According to him, one of the stars of that Super Bowl-winning squad should be inducted into the Hall of Fame.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"My golden ticket, unquestionably, goes to Hines Ward. He's got Hall of Fame numbers. He's got 1,000 career catches, 12,000 yards, 85 touchdowns, and a Super Bowl MVP," said the 54-year-old Tomlin.

"But beyond the statistics, it was his style of play. This guy was a predator, not prey. Every defensive player in the National Football League feared Hines Ward. When you played against Hines Ward, you hated him. No DB (defensive back) liked Hines Ward. He would try to take your head off."

Aside from the numbers he mentioned, Ward was a two-time champion, a three-time All-Pro, and a four-time Pro Bowler. He was named to the Steelers All-Time Team and the Steelers Hall of Honor.

Ward has been nominated for the Hall of Fame for 10 straight years, but he has yet to get the nod. It has been long overdue, and Tomlin made sure to use his platform to bat for the inclusion of his former player.

Tomlin, for his part, also has a strong case to be inducted into the prestigious club in the near future, having won a Vince Lombardi Trophy and recording a 19-year streak of winning seasons.

title: ‘Cardinals Should Name Carson Beck Starting QB’ — Calls Mount for Arizona To Start Rookie Over Jacoby Brissett in Week 1
description: The Hall of Fame Game got off to a hot start, with the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals each putting together nice scoring drives in the first half. The Cardinals started rookie Carson Beck, and he led a brilliant scoring drive pinned deep in his own territory.
fullText:
The Hall of Fame Game got off to a hot start, with the Carolina Panthers and Arizona Cardinals each putting together nice scoring drives in the first half. The Cardinals started rookie Carson Beck, and he led a brilliant scoring drive pinned deep in his own territory. After the drive, the NFL world began to call for the Cardinals to consider Beck as the Week 1 starter.

Beck has looked outstanding in the early parts of the opening preseason game. His play is giving the Cardinals some potential headaches on whether Beck deserves to be the starter ahead of the projected starting QB, Jacoby Brissett, who just got a big pay raise a few weeks ago.

But that's not stopping the noise surrounding Beck's case to win the job.

"Jacoby Brissett watching Carson Beck in the HOF game," said Underdog Fantasy on X while posting a video to mock the veteran quarterback.

Even Sleeper joined in on the fun of trolling the Cardinals' QB competition by indicating that Brissett is sweating after seeing Beck's performance.

The Cardinals just made a big commitment to Brissett with a one-year, $15.5 million guaranteed contract, but if Beck gives them a better chance to win, it would be hard to keep him off the field.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's FREE NFL Mock Draft Simulator

The rookie's strong play has made it tough for members of the NFL world to view this performance as a potential sign of how long Brissett may be allowed to hold a firm grip on the job.

"Jacoby Brissett after forcing the Cardinals to give him a raise just to be benched by week 8," said Matt King, an NFL content creator, while sharing a video.

"Jacoby Brissett will not be the Cardinals' starting QB…at least not for long," added another social media personality.

PFN's accounton X wrote, "Carson Beck is putting on a masterclass in his NFL preseason debut. 🎯 Will the rookie overtake the Cardinals' QB1 job by the end of the season?"

The account shared a graphic showing the Cardinals QB's performance against the Panthers, in which he completed 78.6% of his throws for 148 yards and a touchdown in the first half.

Former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III reacted to Beck's performance, saying, "Carson Beck looking like QB1 for the Arizona Cardinals."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's FREE NFL Playoff Predictor

Former NFL player Breiden Fehoko chimed in on the QB debate in Arizona, with Beck inching closer to getting a real shot.

"Jacoby Brissett, your leash just got a little shorter," said Fehoko.

While some believe that Brissett might have a short leash, others believe that Brissett doesn't deserve this leash at all, despite the monetary commitment.

"Starting Brissett over Beck would be a total waste of time,"said one social media personality.

NFL analyst Chad Forbes has seen enough and is ready to crown Beck the starter before halftime of the Hall of Fame Game.

"I've seen enough. Cardinals should name Carson Beck starting QB tonight. Paying Jacoby Brissett never made any logical sense. Roll with Beck," said Forbes.

The Cardinals may not have invested eight figures on Beck, but using a third-round pick isn't cheap, either. Beck is meant to be a building block for the future, but the future might be now.

It remains to be seen whether Brissett's days as the starter are actually numbered or whether Beck's performance against mostly the Panthers' backups isn't enough to carry weight to sway opinions in Arizona.

title: Jaylen Brown admits that he sees VJ Edgecombe shining amid the discourse about his role
description: After the 76ers' offseason moves, a lot of people were worried about VJ Edgecombe's spot on the team.
fullText:
Jaylen Brown admits that he sees VJ Edgecombe shining amid the discourse about his role originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

After a standout rookie season with the Philadelphia 76ers, VJ Edgecombe became known as one of the biggest stars for the future. He has a natural skill set to become one of the go-to guys in the long run, but it seems he will be playing a smaller role for the foreseeable future.

Even the outspoken Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green called him the "loser" of the offseason for Philly. The four-time champion believes that Edgecombe will have a smaller role, but new 76ers forward Jaylen Brown does not 

As one of the brightest young talents in the league, Edgecombe is an exciting player for the 76ers' future. At the same time, he is also one of their best players today despite being only 21. He has a bright future ahead of him, especially since he will be learning from the likes of Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and LeBron James.

He might have a smaller role this season as more of a 3-and-D player, but that talent will shine through. Edgecombe also has a tremendous personality for an athlete, so he will find ways to assert himself in head coach Nick Nurse's system no matter what happens.

MORE: Draymond Green calls VJ Edgecombe the biggest loser of the 76ers' offseason

Brown talked about this discourse during his introductory press conference on Thursday, August 6. He knows that Edgecombe is hungry to prove himself, so he won't have much of an issue. In fact, Brown does have some type of kinship with Edgecombe because he sees a lot of himself in the youngster.

"VJ is in a similar situation that I was in a couple of years ago. Some of those rosters that were really stacked with talent, and I looked at it like a learning opportunity. I'm going to be in VJ's ear to just learn and grow... He's gonna carve out space for himself with his talent level alone. I'm a fan of VJ," Brown said about Edgecombe's development and new role with the 76ers.

Considering Brown did play alongside the likes of Kyrie Irving, Gordon Hayward, and Jayson Tatum during his time with the Boston Celtics, he knows how to shine in a team full of star players. Edgecombe is in the same boat, and thankfully, he can learn from Brown himself as they are playing alongside each other.

title: Report: Aaron Donald could make decision in the coming days
description: Aaron Donald could decide on a return in the coming days, potentially early enough to play some snaps in Week 1.
fullText:
It may not be long before we find out whether Aaron Donald is coming out of retirement or not. According to Mike Florio of ProFootballTalk, Donald could make a decision about his future in the coming days.

Sean McVay said there would be no update until the team leaves training camp, so Florio's report tracks with that timeline. The Rams will hold their last practice of camp on Friday before returning to Woodland Hills this weekend.

If Donald does decide to come back, Florio says he could be on the field for 30-40 snaps in the Week 1 opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

"If he decides to do it, we could have an announcement within the next few days," Florio said on NBC's pregame show Thursday night. "And if that happens, the Rams would go back to 2017, 2018, he was a training camp holdout, he didn't have much practice. They'll give him a few weeks of on-field activities with his teammates to get him ready for the first game. And the first game is five weeks away in Australia against the 49ers. I'm told, if he comes back, he could get between 30-40 snaps in that debut."

A little Aaron Donald news from HOF pregame. pic.twitter.com/GBDDuRuWZD

Donald has stayed in shape throughout his two-year retirement, and it's likely that all he'd need to get into football shape is a few weeks. He's been ramping up his training in anticipation of this possible comeback, even putting in an official workout with the Rams this week.

The ball has been in his court the whole time, and now we might not have to wait much longer before he decides whether he'll shoot his shot or pass.

title: Former Seahawk Riq Woolen Compares Philadelphia Eagles Culture to Seattle
description: Riq Woolen has a new home with the Eagles after deaparting the Seahawks this offseason, and now he's comparing their team cultures. The post Former Seahawk Riq Woolen Compares Philadelphia Eagles Culture to Seattle appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Training camp is in full bloom around the NFL, and teams are starting to build chemistry and shape what kind of squad they'll be in the upcoming year.

There are new faces in new places that are getting adjusted to their new team and routine. Former Seattle Seahawks cornerback Riq Woolen is one of those players. Woolen signed with the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason on a one-year deal.

Woolen was a bit of a polarizing player at times in Seattle, but he ultimately was an integral part of the Seahawks becoming Super Bowl champions. Now, Woolen is using his experience and lessons learned as a Seahawk to assimilate into the Eagles culture.

The Seahawks and the Eagles have commonalities. They are the last two Super Bowl champions, feature starting quarterbacks who have been doubted for large portions of their careers, and both have bird-based mascots. However, the biggest commonality is between their team cultures, as Riq Woolen has observed in his short time in Philadelphia.

NBC Sports Philadelphia's Reuben Frank wrote about Woolen and his thoughts on Eagles culture and the comparisons to Seahawks culture in his July 31 article.

"Honestly, just the culture here is just an amazing culture. They preach to us we got to work hard," Woolen said. "It's a hard-working team. Everybody in this organization works hard. So just being able to be coached by them, I feel like it's going to help me as a player and it's going to push me to be a great person."

Woolen then brought up the similar hard-working franchise he came from in Seattle.

"I came from an organization that has a similar knack for hard work and a knack for greatness," Woolen continued. "This city here, y'all have a long line of athletes who've made history here, and same thing for Seattle. It all comes from working hard and working as a team. Philly was one of those teams that works hard in a championship caliber."

Despite leaving in free agency, Woolen exited Seattle on good terms, and letting him walk was more financially motivated than anything.

The Seahawks lost several impact players in free agency, from Coby Bryant to Kenneth Walker III to Boye Mafe and Riq Woolen. The downside of having such a great team is you can't afford to pay everyone, and the Seahawks felt that this season.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald explained that the decision not to re-sign Woolen was a financial decision above all else.

"We didn't let him go," Macdonald said to The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar at the NFL's annual league meetings back in March.

"[The Eagles are] getting a great player," Macdonald continued. "We love Riq. He's a great player."

With only so much money to be spread around, John Schneider and the Seahawks had to make tough decisions, and at the time, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Devon Witherspoon extensions on the horizon, Woolen was an odd man out in 2026 for the Seahawks.

Now, though, Woolen has a fresh start in Philadelphia and helps complete one of the best secondaries in the NFL alongside first-team All-Pros Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean.

title: Cardinals rookie QB Carson Beck impresses as he gets first NFL snaps in Hall of Fame Game
description: The NFL got the preseason going on Thursday night with the Hall of Fame Game.
fullText:
At some point this season, the Arizona Cardinals seem likely to get rookie Carson Beck some starts. They gave him one on Thursday to start that process.

And if the rest of the preseason goes as well as Thursday did, the push to get the rookie some regular-season starts might happen earlier than expected.

Beck, a third-round pick who was a college star at Georgia and Miami, started for the Cardinals against the Carolina Panthers as the NFL got the preseason started with the Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio. Beck looked good.

He looked quite comfortable as he took the Cardinals on a 96-yard touchdown drive to end the first quarter. The Cardinals were backed up near their own end zone when Beck made a big play. Receiver Jalen Brooks made a nice double move and Beck hit him downfield for a 35-yard gain. Later in the drive he had a nice pass to Brooks over the middle, delivering an accurate throw despite tight coverage for 15 yards. Beck completed a pass to the 1-yard line and then running back Corey Kiner scored the first unofficial touchdown of the NFL season to start the second quarter.

Carson Beck deep shot on third down 🚀

(via @NFL)pic.twitter.com/lwcAR9TDB3

Beck finished the first quarter 8 of 9 for 81 yards. On Beck's first pass of the second quarter, he threw deep to Brooks, who hauled it in for 49 yards. Beck wasn't nervous about pushing the ball downfield, which is a good sign. Then Beck threw a nice fade route for a third-and-goal touchdown to Simi Fehoko.

Carson Beck throws his first career NFL touchdown for the Cardinals 👏

(via @NFL)pic.twitter.com/cVmC2XNNMv

Beck was playing with and against plenty of players who won't make 53-man rosters, but it was still a promising first game. He played one series in the second half before he was replaced, finishing 15 of 19 for 188 yards. Given how it was the only game of the week after a long offseason, there will surely be plenty of overreaction over Beck's strong performance.

The Cardinals have veterans Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew II on the roster. Brissett will likely begin the season as the starter, but Arizona has a tough early schedule, and at some point the team might want to get a look at Beck. If Arizona finishes with one of the NFL's worst records, as it did last season, the Cardinals will want to know what they have in Beck before entering a 2027 NFL Draft that is deep at quarterback.

Arizona is already invested in Beck. Beck was the 65th overall pick, the first selection of the third round — a valuable pick for a Cardinals team that is in the middle of a rebuild. Clearly Arizona wanted to take a shot on Beck, who helped Georgia and then Miami win a lot of games. He was a productive college quarterback but also had UCL surgery on his elbow during his college career. He threw 12 interceptions in each of his last two seasons, and there were reports before the draft that his personality rubbed teams the wrong way. That's why he slid to the third round, though he did lead off the round.

The Cardinals still have three more preseason games and they'll keep getting Beck reps in preseason games. The first look at him on an NFL field was clearly a positive.

title: Ryan Niblett names the three fastest Texas players, and the results will surprise you
description: A freshman tops the list.
fullText:
AUSTIN, Texas — Access to the Catapult GPS data tracked by the Texas Longhorns coaching staff isn't made accessible to the media or the public, so insight into the fastest players on the team has to come from sourced reporting, high school track times, companies like Reel Analytics that use AI to measure game film, and the players themselves.

On Thursday, following the second practice of preseason camp at Frank Denius Fields, redshirt junior running back/wide receiver Ryan Niblett, the team's dynamic return man, was asked about the three fastest players on the team. His response was surprising, and not just because he excluded himself, citing his humility.

"Kohen, of course," Niblett said. "Kohen's definitely fast."

That's freshman wide receiver Kohen Brown, a surprising pick thanks to his youth and relatively modest recruiting rankings — the Waxahachie product was the No. 266 player nationally and the No. 42 wide receiver in the 247Sports Composite rankings in the 2026 cycle.

With 41 offers, Brown was a coveted prospect when he committed to Texas last summer less than a month after receiving his offer from the Longhorns. And his 100-meter times from his junior season of high school are impressive with a 10.69 effort, but not the best on the team.

But Brown did impress head coach Steve Sarkisian with his physical development over the offseason and reportedly reached 23.1 miles per hour in summer conditioning, a number that Niblett may be referencing in placing Brown atop the team's speed chart.

Brown's speed flashed on a catch from freshman quarterback Dia Bell during the viewing period of Wednesday's practice.

Dia Bell to Kohen Brown. Dot. 🤘 pic.twitter.com/TWw5uZZPrq

Perhaps more impressive was how Brown tracked the ball over his shoulder.

The art of the catch from Texas freshman wide receiver Kohen Brown. Textbook tracking. Sees the ball into the hands. Stays inbounds in the corner of the end zone.

All of the good stuff. All in one reception. pic.twitter.com/TXgU65i9nr

As a true freshman, Brown doesn't project as a contributor on offense, but it may only be a matter of time as his trajectory shows signs of quickly outpacing his rankings.

The second player cited by Niblett was much less surprising — junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo, whose combination of size and speed made him a consensus five-star prospect through most of the 2024 cycle.

It's verified speed, too, as Wingo finished third in the Missouri 5A state championships in the 100 meters as a sophomore with a time of 10.55. After arriving on the Forty Acres, Wingo was one of the 10 fastest players in college football tracked by Reel Analytics last year, reaching 22 miles per hour, which slotted fifth overall, achieved on a post route touchdown catch against Sam Houston.

Fastest 5 College Football Players of Week 4

2️⃣ 22.0 mph – Texas WR Ryan Wingo (@_Ryanwingo1) #ReelSpeed 

🔗 https://t.co/qrL6HYSf3o pic.twitter.com/haDl6RMWga

Senior cornerback Warren Roberson was another surprising inclusion as the third player mentioned by Niblett — while the Red Oak product has surely improved his speed since arriving on the Forty Acres as a member of the 2023 recruiting class, his 100-meter times between 11 seconds and 11.27 seconds as a sophomore came five years ago, with his latest 200-meter time of 23.4 seconds as a junior.

Roberson's speed helps explain why he's been a core special teams player for coordinator Jeff Banks over the last two seasons, totaling 556 snaps on five units, but to build on his 187 snaps on defense last season, the 6'0 , 189-pounder will have to combine that speed with consistent technique and discipline.

There's a good chance he's in the top three after running a 10.58 100-meter dash and a 22.14 200-meter dash as a sophomore at Aldine Eisenhower six years ago.

With the Horns, Niblett hit 20.8 miles per hour on his punt return touchdown against Oklahoma in Week 7 last year, good for eighth nationally that week.

Top 10 Fastest College Football Players of Week 7

8️⃣ 20.8 mph – Ryan Niblett (@ryan_niblett) DB Texas #ReelSpeed 

🔗 https://t.co/qrL6HYSMSW pic.twitter.com/eNyz1w7YTa

title: Arizona Diamondbacks Announce Nolan Arenado Change During Padres Series

fullText:
The Arizona Diamondbacks secured a dominant 10-4 victory over the San Diego Padres on Wednesday night.

Ahead of Thursday night's series finale, manager Torey Lovullo made several notable lineup changes after both Ketel Marte and Nolan Arenado sat out Game 3 of the series.

After receiving a day off, Arenado returns to the lineup for the series finale, starting at third base and batting sixth.

Marte also returns to the starting nine and will start at second base while hitting cleanup.

Other notable tweaks from Lovullo include moving Geraldo Perdomo into the leadoff spot, dropping Lars Nootbaar lower in the lineup while shifting him from the outfield to designated hitter, and inserting Max Kepler into the starting lineup after he didn't start Wednesday.

Here's the full Diamondbacks lineup:

 C. Carroll RF
 G. Moreno C
 K. Marte 2B
 L. Nootbaar DH

 M. Kepler LF
 T. Tawa 1B
 R. Waldschmidt CF

â Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) August 6, 2026

Arenado is in his 14th MLB season but his first with the Diamondbacks, and the eight-time All-Star continues to produce at a high level.

Through 108 games and 369 at-bats, Arenado is batting .244 with 53 runs, 90 hits, 16 home runs and 53 RBIs while slugging .428 and posting a .754 OPS.

Arizona enters Thursday with a 61-54 record, sitting second in the NL West, 8.0 games behind the Los Angeles Dodgers.

The Diamondbacks have won six of their last eight games, and if the season ended today, they would hold the second National League Wild Card spot. That would set up a best-of-three Wild Card Series against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field.

The Philadelphia Phillies, who currently hold the third and final Wild Card spot, are tied with Arizona in the standings. Both teams lead the San Diego Padres by 2.0 games as they battle for the final two playoff spots.

title: ‘Sold the game’: Criticism rises against Caitlin Clark after she gets ‘punked’ to lose game
description: The Indiana Fever are doing their best to keep the focus on basketball, following weeks of controversy tied to comments reserve guard Sophie Cunningham made about transgender athletes participating in women’s sports. After initially doubling down, Cunningham is now calling for the media to recenter the conversation around the team on basketball. “There is so…
fullText:
The Indiana Fever are doing their best to keep the focus on basketball, following weeks of controversy tied to comments reserve guard Sophie Cunningham made about transgender athletes participating in women's sports. After initially doubling down, Cunningham is now calling for the media to recenter the conversation around the team on basketball.

"There is so much good going on in the WNBA. I think basketball is being played at the highest level it's ever been," Cunningham told WISH-TV News in Indianapolis. "There's just so much distraction. The WNBA media, all we ever do is cover everything except basketball. It's like, what are we doing? You can talk about other things; I think those are great stories. It shows fans who people are outside of the court, but I also think we gotta keep the main thing the main thing."

"I want to get back to basketball; it's always been about basketball," she insisted. "That interview happened in February when I was asked a question. And for me, I just want to make sure the focus stays where it should."

The Fever faced off against the Las Vegas Aces on Thursday, and although the team may be working on eliminating distractions as the playoffs draw nearer, one player was clearly off her A game. Clark finished the game with 20 points and 8 assists, but struggled immensely with her efficiency, shooting 7-for-20 from the field, including 2-for-10 from the three-point line. Her struggles in the game were not wasted on fans watching from home.

"Caitlin Clark is one of the funniest players in the league cuz to every casual she is the Greatest Player ever but to anyone who actually keeps up with the WNBA knows she has 1 good game a month lmao," one fan posted on X.

"I find it so fascinating that Caitlin Clark remains the face of the WNBA despite not even being a top 5 player in the league," another person added.

Clark also missed two free throws late to clinch a win in regulation, and fans let her hear it for that as well.

"Caitlin Clark choke job," one fan wrote.

"Caitlin Clark sold the f*cking game with the dumb*ss missed two FTs! Trash!!!" someone else added.

Clark then had the game-losing turnover, as it led to a buzzer-beater game-winning three-pointer by Aces point guard Chelsea Gray.

"Aja Wilson just punked Caitlin Clark for game," one fan put bluntly.

Even though it wasn't her best outing, Clark managed to leave a massive impact on the game. If this is her floor, the Fever franchise is in extremely good shape.

title: Cardinals QB Depth Chart: Could rookie Carson Beck's impressive NFL debut create competition in Arizona?
description: Here's a breakdown of how Beck could climb the Cardinals' depth chart if his strong preseason play continues.
fullText:
Cardinals QB Depth Chart: Could rookie Carson Beck's impressive NFL debut create competition in Arizona? originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Hall of Fame Game doesn't usually feature big names, but Thursday's contest between the Arizona Cardinals and Carolina Panthers marked the NFL debut of a former college star.

Carson Beck, who started three collegiate seasons at Georgia and Miami, got the start for the Cardinals in the season's first preseason game. The third-round pick got the nod over two veterans, hoping to prove he deserves playing time.

Beck then went on to put up some impressive tape and lead Arizona to 17 points in the first half. With the Cardinals not particularly flush with quarterback talent, Beck could find himself on the field sooner rather than later.

Here's a breakdown of how Beck could climb the Cardinals' depth chart.

MORE:NFL offseason grades for all 32 teams

Beck should enter the season as the third-string quarterback behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew, but he could have the chance to earn some playing time anyway. The Cardinals are not expected to be that good, so the team could turn to Beck later in the season if the year is out of hand.

For now, Beck will likely be a healthy scratch on game days while fighting to earn time as the primary backup. Both Brissett and Minshew are well-travelled veterans, but neither is entrenched as the team's starter beyond this year.

MORE:The NFL's 25 highest-paid players in 2026

Beck has a strong performance in the Hall of Fame game, producing 148 passing yards in a half of action. He had two highlight plays, both of which were deep completions to wide receiver Jalen Brooks.

What a throw by Carson Beck!@ProFootballHOF Game on NBC
Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/ai2A4lm7z0

Carson Beck to Jalen Brooks. WOW.@ProFootballHOF Game on NBC
Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/VjnMEP2mIQ

Beck then threw for his first NFL touchdown to wide receiver Simi Fehoko in the second quarter.

.@carsonbeck01 drops it in a bucket 🪣@ProFootballHOF Game on NBC
Stream on @NFLPlus + Peacock pic.twitter.com/fZQpMPha1q

Beck spent six seasons in college, five of which were with Georgia and one with Miami. He was the Bulldogs' primary backup in both 2021 and 2022, when Georgia won back-to-back national titles, then took over as the starter in 2023 for two seasons. Beck transferred to Miami in 2025, making it three straight years as a starter.

Over his span as a starter from 2023 to 2025, Beck played in 42 games and totaled 82 touchdowns and more than 900 completions.

Beck is 24 years-old and will turn 25 in November, making him one of the older rookies in the NFL this year. Still, he is the youngest quarterback on the Cardinals' depth chart as both Brissett and Minshew are at least 30 years-old, while Slovis is 25.

title: Mavs 'very resistant' to buy out Klay Thompson due to Lakers' interest
description: Per one insider, the Mavericks "have been very resistant" to buy out Klay Thompson's contract because the Lakers reportedly are interested in him.
fullText:
A few days ago, a report came out that indicated Klay Thompson of the Dallas Mavericks "would welcome a return to Los Angeles," a metropolitan area where he spent his high school years. The NBA world interpreted this report as Thompson having some desire to come to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Thompson, who is 36 years of age, is entering the final year of a three-year, $50 million contract he signed with Dallas in 2024 shortly after leaving the Golden State Warriors. He, of course, won four NBA championships with the Warriors and had been drafted by them with the No. 11 pick in the 2011 draft.

Insider Jake Fischer said on a Bleacher Report video that the Mavericks "have been very resistant" to buying out Thompson's contract since there is interest in him on the market.

"To this point, Dallas has not been looking to find a buyout agreement with Klay Thompson. He's got one year left on a three-year, $51 million deal that he signed two seasons ago when he left the Golden State Warriors, the franchise he won four championships with, of course…Klay Thompson very nearly chose the Los Angeles Lakers with then LeBron James over joining Dallas originally to pair with Luka Doncic and where's Luka Doncic right now? Of course, with the Lakers. There's plenty of connective tissue there that makes sense here. The only thing is, the Mavericks have been very resistant, to my understanding, of actually moving forward and agreeing to a buyout with Klay Thompson. They believe this market that's shaping up for him, the fact that there is some LA interest, the fact that there is Miami interest. There's probably other places that have interest in Klay Thompson as well."

While Fischer implied that the Lakers could have interest in Thompson, it is unknown how much interest they actually have in him.

At this point in his career, the five-time All-Star is a below-average defender and lacks athleticism and mobility, especially on the defensive end. In his heyday, he was regarded as a strong defender and was named to the All-Defensive second team in 2019, but the ACL injury he suffered in 2019 and the subsequent Achilles tear he sustained in 2020 robbed him of a lot of his natural ability.

Even Thompson's 3-point accuracy, his biggest superpower, has dropped off a bit in recent years. He shot above 40% from 3-point range in each of his first eight NBA seasons, but he has been below that mark in four of the last five years. But he still shot 38.3% from downtown on 7.6 attempts in 21.7 minutes a game last season, so he could still have something to offer, albeit in limited playing time.

title: Warriors Get Intriguing Anthony Davis Update Amid Stephen Curry Decision
description: Golden State passed on an aggressive Anthony Davis pursuit this summer, but two looming contract decisions could change the conversation. The post Warriors Get Intriguing Anthony Davis Update Amid Stephen Curry Decision appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Anthony Davis is not available. At least not yet.

The Washington Wizards have given no indication they intend to trade him, and the Golden State Warriors did not come particularly close to acquiring him when they explored the possibility earlier this offseason.

Still, Davis' future suddenly carries more uncertainty than it did when Washington shut down trade interest in June.

The Wizards and Davis have mutually agreed to table negotiations on a potential four-year, $275 million extension until the regular season, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday on NBA Today. One source told Charania the sides want to let approximately 20 games "marinate" before deciding whether their partnership should continue through a new contract.

For Golden State, the development is worth monitoring. Its championship window around Stephen Curry continues to narrow, and Davis was central to the Warriors' most ambitious offseason scenario before LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.

GettyStephen Curry of the Golden State Warriors shoots over Anthony Davis and LeBron James of the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on January 27, 2024 in San Francisco, California.

Golden State planned to pursue James in free agency and explore a trade for Davis, Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor reported in June. Washington had no interest in listening to offers, preventing those plans from gaining traction.

The Warriors also had internal reservations. According to The Ringer's Logan Murdock, a small group within Golden State's front office supported trading Jimmy Butler and draft capital for Davis. The organization ultimately declined to push forward because of Davis' injury history and desire for a lucrative extension.

Davis' fit beside Curry remains obvious. His screening, lob finishing and ability to punish switches would give Curry an elite pick-and-roll partner. Defensively, Davis could protect the rim while allowing Draymond Green to roam, switch and direct traffic.

Davis averaged 20.4 points, 11.1 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 20 games for Dallas last season. But hand and groin injuries ended his campaign before he could debut for Washington, reinforcing the concerns that kept Golden State from making a more aggressive push.

If Davis becomes available, Golden State cannot assemble a deal from spare contracts.

Butler's expiring $56.8 million salary is the Warriors' only clean, single-contract match for Davis, who will earn approximately $58.4 million this season. That financial reality — not necessarily a demand from Washington — would make Butler the practical foundation of almost any Davis trade.

The alternative would be a more complicated package constructed around the combined salaries of Green and Kristaps Porziņģis.

Green re-signed on a one-year, $27.7 million contract after opting out to help Golden State pursue James. Although signing a one-year deal created implicit veto rights, Green waived that protection in favor of a 15% trade kicker, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater. He becomes eligible to be traded Dec. 15 and would receive a bonus of approximately $4.2 million if moved.

The Warriors have maintained that they do not intend to trade Green. His contract, however, preserves their ability to do so if a franchise-altering opportunity emerges.

That flexibility matters because Curry's future is also approaching a decision point. The 38-year-old guard is under contract only through 2026-27 and becomes eligible Aug. 29 for a two-year extension worth up to approximately $136.7 million. ESPN has reported mutual interest in another agreement.

But Curry's contract cannot be separated entirely from the roster around him. Butler is recovering from a torn ACL, Green is 36, and Golden State won only 37 games last season.

Washington's first 20 games will determine whether Davis fits alongside Trae Young, Alex Sarr and AJ Dybantsa. They could also determine whether Golden State gets another opportunity to make the aggressive move it passed on this summer.

This time, the Warriors would know exactly where the money must come from.

title: “I’m Gonna Try to Hold Him Off”: Kirk Cousins Determined to Delay Fernando Mendoza’s Debut Amid Raiders QB Battle
description: Kirk Cousins is not just holding the Las Vegas Raiders‘ starting quarterback job at camp; he made it clear that he intends to keep it for as long as he possibly can. Sharing a quarterback room with the No.
fullText:
Kirk Cousins is not just holding the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback job at camp; he made it clear that he intends to keep it for as long as he possibly can. Sharing a quarterback room with the No. 1 overall pick of this year's draft does not change that mindset one bit.

"I think the organization is positioned well having drafted Fernando [Mendoza]," he told ESPN's Dan Graziano. "I'm gonna try to hold him off as long as I can, and we'll see how it goes up ahead."

It's a blunt admission from a 37-year-old veteran, who is still regarded by many as a transitional quarterback for the team. Mendoza is the presumed franchise quarterback, and Kirk Cousins has only been signed for two years. However, Cousins had set the record straight: he is not here to only mentor the rookie.

"I think to say I'm mentoring them is a bit of a reach, probably more of a narrative than it is the truth," he said in June. "They're pretty good players and pretty experienced, and I'm learning a lot from them too and asking questions of them."

Get The Huddle Newsletter. The day's biggest NFL stories — rivalries, matchups, expert analysis, power rankings, and insider draft news.

Cousins echoed the same thought in his chat with Graziano.

"You can do both. We're all helping each other, and you kind of compete with each other, I would say more than against. So it should be a good year."

Mendoza's road to the field is not straightforward. OTAs and minicamp were rough. He missed throws and struggled against the defense. Then camp opened and something clicked. He came in showing sharper command of the huddle, quicker decisions, and offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko noticed immediately, praising how fast he is turning what he learns in meetings into real execution on the field.

Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer reported that two things will determine whether Mendoza actually sees real action this season: his readiness to run the offense, and whether the roster around him can protect and support him well enough to give him a chance. Right now neither one is fully there yet.

Kirk Cousins looks like the steadier option for now, which is why he has been named the starting quarterback. He opened camp throwing touchdowns to Jalen Nailor and Brock Bowers, and coaches have praised the collaborative tone he's set in the room. Still, his own words suggest he knows the job isn't guaranteed for long.

"You're only as good as your last throw, your last practice. You try to every day go out and earn that opportunity and never take anything for granted," Cousins said.

Cousins signed with the Raiders back in April, reuniting with head coach Klint Kubiak, who coached him as both quarterbacks coach and offensive coordinator during their years together with the Minnesota Vikings. That relationship, Cousins said, was the biggest reason the move made sense in the first place.

For now, the plan is simple. Cousins holds the job, Mendoza develops behind him, and Kubiak gets to build his offense around a veteran he trusts while his long-term quarterback waits his turn.

title: South Africa coach Erasmus wary of struggling Argentina
description: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus insists the world champions face a "massive challenge" against Argentina on Saturday despite the recent poor form of their opponents. "Argentina are a quality outfit and we are preparing for a physical and gruelling battle," said Erasmus, a key coaching figure in the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cup triumphs of South Africa.
fullText:
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus insists the world champions face a "massive challenge" against Argentina on Saturday despite the recent poor form of their opponents.

The Springboks stretched a winning Test run to 11 matches with home victories over England, Scotland and Wales during July in the inaugural Nations Championship.

Facing the same northen hemisphere teams in South America, the Pumas beat Wales, but lost to Scotland, and England in an ill-tempered clash.

Argentina thought they had scored a late try against England, giving them a chance to draw the Test.

When Australian referee Angus Gardner disallowed it after a lengthy review, Pumas fly-half Tomas Albornoz was furious.

The playmaker had to be physically restrained by a teammate and coaches as he remonstrated with the match official and has since been banned for four matches, starting with the Springboks.

However, the absence of the outstanding playmaker and goal-kicker has not soothed the nerves of Erasmus ahead of the one-off Test at the Estadio Jose Amalfitani in the Argentine capital.

"Argentina are a quality outfit and we are preparing for a physical and gruelling battle," said Erasmus, a key coaching figure in the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cup triumphs of South Africa.

"They are a well coached team who have tested us in the last few years, so it will be a good challenge for us.

"They gave us one of the biggest hidings we have suffered since I became involved with the Springboks in 2018."

Erasmus said he was unhappy that the international had been called a warm-up match for South Africa ahead of a four-Test home series against New Zealand from August 22.

"This match was not planned with that reason in mind -- it was always about honouring our relationship with Argentina," he insisted.

Because of the All Blacks tour, the annual Rugby Championship southern hemisphere tournament, which includes two matches between the Springboks and Pumas, has been scrapped this year.

South Africa are fielding an experimental team, containing just five probable starters for the first New Zealand Test.

The match marks the return following injuries of fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, locks Eben Etzebeth and Lood de Jager and captain and flanker Siya Kolisi.

Only two of the team that started a 43-0 romp against Wales in Durban -- full-back Aphelele Fassi and scrum-half Cobus Reinach -- keep their places.

Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi has handed a starting debut to tighthead prop Francisco Moreno.

Hooker Leonel Oviedo and back-row pair Juan Penoucos and Juan Martin Scelzo could earn their first Test caps from the bench.

title: Chris Finch explains why Minnesota felt it needed LaMelo Ball to unlock Anthony Edwards
description: Edwards can return to a more natural role working off the ball now.
fullText:
The Minnesota Timberwolves made a massive pivot this offseason — they went from a big, defense-first team hoping to get enough offense from Anthony Edwards to win, to becoming a high-flying offensive team hoping they can get enough defense to win big. It was a pivot the Timberwolves had to make — they had hit the ceiling with the current construction. If they were going to break on through, it was going to require big changes.

After a blockbuster offseason trade, the Timberwolves may have the most dynamic backcourt in the NBA with Ball and Edwards. In an appearance on the Road Trippin Podcast with Richard Jefferson, Channing Frye and Kendrick Perkins, Minnesota head coach Chris Finch laid out why the franchise felt it had to do this (hat tip Bleacher Report).

"We probably did Anthony a disservice last year, at times, playing him as a point guard. It caught up to us. He did a really great job, but in the playoffs it was just double team after double team. We got to get him back to his natural position off the ball. We didn't create enough catch-and-shoot threes for him and when you look at the numbers with LaMelo on the floor with his teammates and the efficiency and the production, I mean Kon Knueppel shot seven percent higher from the three-point line with LaMelo on the floor than he did without... And obviously LaMelo's a phenomenal talent all by himself. We needed the connective tissue. We needed the point guard play."

Edwards is poised for a massive season, for my money maybe getting into the top five in MVP voting. Finch is spot on that teams last season — especially in the playoffs — could absolutely load up on Edwards and not fear repercussions. That is not the case now. Plus, with Ball, the Timberwolves should play much faster, leading to more easy buckets.

There are a lot of questions. Ball himself is not playoff-tested (he had 30 points in the play-in game against Miami but needed 31 shots to get there, then struggled in a play-in loss to Orlando). There is the defense, which is going to ask a lot of Gobert. This is a very different team than we had seen in Minnesota before, what will be its personality?

What the Timberwolves will be is very fun to watch. And LaMelo in town is going to be good for Ant. Very good.

title: Florida State transfer SF Chauncey Wiggins commits to Gonzaga after judge’s order
description: Florida State transfer forward Chauncey Wiggins has committed to Gonzaga, according to On3’s Joe Tipton. He played the 2026 season at FSU after transferring from Clemson, but entered the transfer portal this cycle. Wiggins was a player to watch for a potential fifth year of eligibility, On3 previously reported. A Colorado judge granted a class-wide […]
fullText:
Florida State transfer forward Chauncey Wiggins has committed to Gonzaga, according to On3's Joe Tipton. He played the 2026 season at FSU after transferring from Clemson, but entered the transfer portal this cycle.

Wiggins was a player to watch for a potential fifth year of eligibility, On3 previously reported. A Colorado judge granted a class-wide preliminary injunction last week, which declared the Class of 2022 eligible for the 2026 season pending an NCAA appeal, opened the door for him to possibly return to college basketball.

$19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage

The judge's order stated players who were returning could only play for their previous team, meaning they could not enter the portal outside of the window. However, Wiggins hit the open market in April after one season at FSU.

Chauncey Wiggins appeared in 32 games for Florida State last season, including 30 starts. He averaged a career-high 13.3 points while adding 3.9 rebounds per game, as well. That came after three seasons at Clemson, where he took on a starting role in 2024-25 when he started 26 out of 34 games played. That season, Wiggins averaged 8.3 points and 2.9 rebounds.

Judge Charlotte Sweeney's order came after the NCAA announced the implementation of its 5-year, age-based eligibility rule. Under the new guidelines, athletes will have a five-year eligibility clock beginning with their 19th birthday or when they enroll in college, whichever occurs sooner. However, athletes from the Class of 2022 – which just completed their fourth seasons – would not be "grandfathered" in under the new rules.

As a result, the NCAA faced multiple lawsuits, and Sweeney's ruling was for the entire class. However, she later clarified her ruling and said the transfer rules would not enjoined, meaning those athletes could not enter the portal. Additionally, roster limits in place under the House v. NCAA settlement also remain in effect, meaning schools cannot go beyond that figure if athletes decide to come back.

"The Court's order does not enjoin the operation of transfer rules," Sweeney wrote in the order, issued Aug. 2. "As the plain language of the preliminary injunction order and this order make clear, the Court's injunction concerns only the implementation of the Rule (as defined in the preliminary injunction order) and any Bylaw that prohibits Plaintiffs and Class Members from competing in a fifth season of collegiate athletics."

While a major decision, Sweeney's ruling is not necessarily final. The NCAA, as expected, is appealing it and hoping for a stay of the injunction. The governing body also issued a clarification which stated any athlete who signed a pro contract will not be eligible under terms of the judge's order.

title: Chelsea Gray forces OT and ends OT with buzzer-beaters as Aces overcome 20-point deficit to beat Fever
description: The Fever led by 3 points when the regulation buzzer sounded and by 2 points at the overtime buzzer. They lost.
fullText:
Thursday's game between the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever was billed as a playoff preview. Chelsea Gray was more than ready.

The Aces star point guard delivered not one, but two buzzer-beating 3-pointers in one of the wildest games of the WNBA season, lifting the Aces to an 86-84 win. There were 12 lead changes overall in the game, and the final one came as time expired to silence the Indiana crowd.

A'ja Wilson steal and then CHELSEA GRAY DOES IT AGAIN! This time it's a game winner. Insane. pic.twitter.com/lAG8uTxmWC

Previously, the Fever had the ball with 30 seconds left and a one-point lead, with a chance to pull away from the Aces. Their possession turned into an iso between two of the league's biggest stars in Caitlin Clark and A'ja Wilson.

It wound up being the four-time MVP's moment, as she stayed in front of the guard at the perimeter and ultimately batted a pass meant for the paint into the air. The makeshift jump ball resulted in contact that sent Clark to the floor, but no foul was called.

Wilson got the ball and gave it to Gray, who went back-and-forth with Jackie Young before calling game.

In regulation, the Fever built up a 20-point lead in the second quarter, only for the Aces to make close the first half with a 15-0 run, then open the second half with a 7-0 run. It was a tug of way from there, with Aces taking a three-point lead in the minute, but then Gray made what turned out to be only her second-biggest shot of the game.

WITH NO TIME REMAINING 🫣

Sheesh, Point Gawd...tell us how you really feel! https://t.co/ecQbsrqInq pic.twitter.com/kdqLT18mKP

Wilson led the Aces with 26 points on 10-of-25 shooting plus 13 rebounds, 3 assists and 2 blocks, while Gray finished with 11 points on 4-of-10 shooting and seven assists.

It was the usual trio leading the Fever, with Kelsey Mitchell (28 points), Aliyah Boston (21 points, 12 rebounds, 3 steals, 2 blocks) and Caitlin Clark (20 points, 8 assists) all showing out. The rest of the Aces combined for 15 points.
